name: Kaohsiung
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Kaohsiung: port and trade counterparties, semiconductor supply chain diligence and court asset research.
hero_lede: Kaohsiung is Taiwan's largest port and its heavy-industry centre, now adding a major semiconductor cluster around TSMC's Nanzih fabs. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for matters touching the city, coordinating Taiwanese counsel and appropriately licensed local professionals where enquiries on the ground are needed.
intro: Kaohsiung is Taiwan's principal southern city and special municipality, with about 2.77 million residents across 38 districts as reported by the city government. Its economy was built on petrochemicals, steel and shipbuilding, and it remains Taiwan's centre for heavy industry, while also producing around 80 percent of the island's yachts. The Port of Kaohsiung is Taiwan's largest international commercial harbour, handling roughly 9.6 to 9.9 million TEU a year in the early 2020s. The Kaohsiung Export Processing Zone, opened in 1966, was Taiwan's first. Since 2022 TSMC has been building five fabs at the Nanzih Technology Industrial Park on the site of a former CPC refinery, anchoring a southern semiconductor corridor that links Kaohsiung with Tainan and Pingtung.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Kaohsiung because the city sits where Taiwan's physical supply chains meet its trade routes. Shipowners, traders and lenders need assurance about counterparties moving cargo, fuel and steel through the port. The build-out of semiconductor capacity draws contractors, equipment suppliers, materials vendors and land deals, each with integrity, trade secret and export control questions. Long-established family groups in steel, petrochemicals, construction and fishing hold assets that become relevant in acquisitions, joint ventures and enforcement. When disputes arise, the Kaohsiung District Court, the Taiwan High Court Kaohsiung Branch and arbitration are the usual routes, with Mandarin and Taiwanese Hokkien sources often essential.

matters.title: Port and shipping counterparties
matters.text: Charterers, cargo owners and financiers dealing with Kaohsiung-based shipping, bunkering and trading firms need to know who controls them and how they have performed. We combine company registration data, court judgments, vessel and trade records and Chinese-language media to identify ownership, related parties and prior disputes.

matters.title: Semiconductor supply chain diligence
matters.text: The Nanzih semiconductor build-out involves construction contractors, equipment and materials suppliers and service firms, many newly established or expanding. We verify their registration, directors, shareholders reported publicly, litigation and reputational record, and look for connections that raise conflict of interest, trade secret or export control concerns.

matters.title: Trade secret and employee departures
matters.text: Technology and heavy-industry employers in Kaohsiung face the risk of staff leaving with confidential process knowledge. Working with Taiwanese counsel, we research the new employer, corporate links and public records relevant to suspected misappropriation, supporting decisions on civil or criminal steps under Taiwan's trade secrets regime.

matters.title: Family groups and joint ventures
matters.text: Kaohsiung's industrial, construction and fishing businesses are often controlled by families through networks of companies. Before a joint venture or acquisition we map the group from MOEA registration data, listed company disclosures and judgments, and assess succession disputes, guarantees and political connections.

matters.title: Asset research for enforcement
matters.text: Creditors with judgments or arbitral awards against southern Taiwanese parties need to know what is reachable. We map companies, listed shareholdings, real estate reported through lawful channels and assets held abroad, so that counsel can plan provisional attachment and enforcement through the Kaohsiung District Court.

local_context.title: Kaohsiung District Court
local_context.text: The Taiwan Kaohsiung District Court, established in December 1945, is the first-instance court for civil, criminal and non-contentious cases across much of the city, and hears second-instance summary cases. It is the usual forum for commercial disputes below the threshold for the Intellectual Property and Commercial Court, and for provisional attachment and enforcement against local assets. Northern districts fall partly within the Ciaotou District Court, and family matters go to the Kaohsiung Juvenile and Family Court. Judgments are published through the Judicial Yuan's online system.

local_context.title: Taiwan High Court Kaohsiung Branch
local_context.text: The Taiwan High Court Kaohsiung Branch Court hears appeals from the Kaohsiung, Ciaotou, Pingtung and Penghu District Courts and the Kaohsiung Juvenile and Family Court. Its territory, which covers Kaohsiung City, Pingtung and Penghu counties and the outlying Dongsha and Taiping islands, is described by the court as the largest of any High Court branch. Larger commercial cases involving public companies or high claim values go instead to the Intellectual Property and Commercial Court in Taipei.

local_context.title: Export processing and industrial zones
local_context.text: The Kaohsiung Export Processing Zone, opened in 1966, was Taiwan's first, and Kaohsiung also hosts the Nanzih zone and the headquarters of the export processing zone administration. Originally home to light assembly industries, the zones now mainly serve technology and electronics operations. Firms in the zones operate under customs and investment rules of their own, and zone administration records, tenancy and import-export patterns can be relevant when assessing a manufacturer or supplier located there.

local_context.title: Port authority and maritime records
local_context.text: The Port of Kaohsiung is operated by Taiwan International Ports Corporation under the Maritime and Port Bureau. Terminal concessions, including the new No. 7 container terminal leased to Evergreen Marine, and port service licences generate public information on operators. For trade and maritime investigations, port, vessel and customs-related information is combined with company records, court judgments and international shipping databases, and is interpreted with Taiwanese maritime counsel where liability or arrest of vessels is in issue.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Kaohsiung and works on Kaohsiung matters from Nashville. We agree the objective with the client and its Taiwanese counsel, whether vetting a port or shipping counterparty, a semiconductor supplier, a joint venture partner or assets for enforcement, and scope the research to it. Sources include MOEA company registration data, listed company disclosures, Judicial Yuan judgments, zone and port information and Chinese-language media, reviewed by native Mandarin readers. We respect Taiwan's Personal Data Protection Act and do not seek restricted beneficial ownership or tax filings. Where interviews or site observation are justified, we coordinate appropriately qualified local professionals after counsel has reviewed the method.

faqs.q: Which court hears a commercial dispute with a Kaohsiung company?
faqs.a: Most claims start in the Taiwan Kaohsiung District Court, or the Ciaotou District Court for some northern districts, with appeals to the Taiwan High Court Kaohsiung Branch. Major commercial disputes involving public companies or claims above the statutory threshold go to the Intellectual Property and Commercial Court in Taipei. Parties may also agree to arbitration. Taiwanese counsel advises on the forum.

faqs.q: Can we check a Kaohsiung supplier's ownership?
faqs.a: Company registration records searchable through the Ministry of Economic Affairs show registered capital, address, representative and directors and supervisors. Filings of major shareholders under the Company Act are made to an MOEA platform but, to our understanding, are not publicly searchable. We combine registration data with judgments, listed company disclosures and media to build a reliable picture of control.

faqs.q: How do you vet contractors around the Nanzih semiconductor projects?
faqs.a: We verify registration and directors, review court judgments and administrative penalties, examine related companies and media coverage, and look for links to employees of the client or to competitors. The aim is to identify integrity, trade secret and capacity concerns before contracts are awarded or expanded, using only lawful public sources.

faqs.q: Can TDSC investigate a cargo or trade finance fraud through Kaohsiung port?
faqs.a: Yes, as a consulting engagement. We trace the counterparties behind the transaction, check company and court records, examine vessel and shipping information and identify related entities in Taiwan and abroad. Where evidence needs to be preserved or a vessel arrested, Taiwanese maritime counsel takes the procedural steps and we support them with research.

faqs.q: Do you conduct surveillance in Kaohsiung?
faqs.a: No. TDSC does not conduct surveillance or fieldwork itself in Taiwan, and Taiwan's personal data and privacy rules limit how information about individuals may be collected. Where local enquiries are justified, we coordinate appropriately qualified Taiwanese professionals and agree the method with counsel first. Most Kaohsiung engagements rely on public records and Chinese-language research.
